jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}本[ほん]{や|ya-list}ノート{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are books, notebooks and so on on the desk.
why: など closes a list of examples and leaves room for more items.

jp: スーパー{で|de-place}野菜[やさい]{や|ya-list}果物[くだもの]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: I bought vegetables, fruit and so on at the supermarket.
why: など follows the last example of an open list, before the object marker.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-topic}友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}映画[えいが]{や|ya-list}買[か]い物[もの]{など|nado-etc}{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: On Sundays I go to the movies, shopping and so on with friends.
why: など ends the list of examples, and the purpose marker follows.

jp: 好[す]きな食[た]べ物[もの]{は|wa-topic}すし{や|ya-list}てんぷら{など|nado-etc}です。
en: My favourite foods are sushi, tempura and so on.
why: など marks sushi and tempura as examples, not the complete list.

jp: お茶[ちゃ]{など/とか|nado-etc}いかがです{か|ka-question}。
en: Would you like some tea or something?
why: など after a single noun offers it as one example, softly.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}電車[でんしゃ]{や|ya-list}バス{など|nado-etc}{で|de-means}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: I go to school by train, bus or the like.
why: など after the last example means there are other means too.

jp: 今日[きょう]{の|no-possessive}宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}漢字[かんじ]{や|ya-list}作文[さくぶん]{など|nado-etc}です。
en: Today's homework is kanji, composition and so on.
why: など presents kanji and composition as examples of the homework.

jp: かばん{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{に|ni-location}財布[さいふ]{や|ya-list}カメラ{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-subject}入[はい]っています。
en: A wallet, a camera and other things are in the bag.
why: など after the last item shows the bag holds more than these.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}「忙[いそが]しい」{など|nado-etc}{と|to-quote}言[い]っ{て|te-sequence}、来[き]ませんでした。
en: He said things like "I'm busy" and didn't come.
why: など before と quotes a sample of what he said, such as 忙しい.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}掃除[そうじ]{や|ya-list}洗濯[せんたく]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}毎日[まいにち]します。
en: Mr. Yamada does cleaning, laundry and so on every day.
why: など lists cleaning and laundry as examples of his chores.

jp: 朝[あさ]{は|wa-topic}パン{や|ya-list}卵[たまご]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: In the morning I eat bread, eggs and so on.
why: など marks bread and eggs as typical examples, not everything.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]{の|no-possessive}とき、地図[ちず]{や|ya-list}カメラ{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}持[も]っ{て|te-sequence}行[い]きます。
en: When I travel, I take a map, a camera and so on.
why: など ends the list of items to take without claiming it is complete.

jp: この町[まち]{に|ni-location}公園[こうえん]{や|ya-list}図書館[としょかん]{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are parks, a library and so on in this town.
why: など follows the last example in an open list of facilities.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{に|ni-location}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{や|ya-list}卵[たまご]{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There's milk, eggs and so on in the fridge.
why: など shows milk and eggs are examples of what is in there.

jp: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}読書[どくしょ]{や|ya-list}料理[りょうり]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}し{て|te-sequence}過[す]ごします。
en: On days off I spend my time reading, cooking and so on.
why: など presents reading and cooking as examples of activities.

jp: テニス{や|ya-list}サッカー{など|nado-etc}{が/は|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: I like tennis, soccer and the like.
why: など after soccer marks both sports as examples of what I like.

jp: ここ{で|de-place}写真[しゃしん]{や|ya-list}ビデオ{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}撮[と]っ{ては|te-wa}いけません。
en: You must not take photos, videos and so on here.
why: など makes photos and videos examples of what is banned.

jp: 佐藤[さとう]さん{は|wa-topic}ピアノ{など|nado-etc}{も|mo-also}上手[じょうず]です。
en: Mr. Sato is also good at things like the piano.
why: など after a single noun gives it as an example; も then adds "also".

jp: 子[こ]どものころ、サッカー{や|ya-list}野球[やきゅう]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}よくしました。
en: As a child I often played soccer, baseball and so on.
why: など ends the list of sports as examples before the object marker.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{に|ni-recipient}花[はな]{や|ya-list}本[ほん]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}あげました。
en: I gave my friend flowers, books and so on.
why: など marks flowers and books as examples of the gifts.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]、ご飯[はん]{や|ya-list}みそ汁[しる]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: My mother makes rice, miso soup and so on every day.
why: など ends the open list of dishes before the object marker.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}肉[にく]{や|ya-list}魚[さかな]{など|nado-etc}{は|wa-negative}食[た]べません。
en: My younger brother doesn't eat meat, fish or the like.
why: など lists meat and fish as examples, and the negative covers them all.

jp: 試験[しけん]{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]、えんぴつ{や|ya-list}消[け]しゴム{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}持[も]っ{て|te-sequence}来[き]ました。
en: On exam day I brought pencils, erasers and so on.
why: など marks pencils and erasers as examples of what I brought.

jp: リビング{に|ni-location}ソファー{や|ya-list}テレビ{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-existence}置[お]いてあります。
en: A sofa, a TV and other things have been put in the living room.
why: など ends the list of furniture, hinting there is more.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}ギター{や|ya-list}ピアノ{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}弾[ひ]きます。
en: My older brother plays the guitar, the piano and so on.
why: など shows the guitar and piano are examples of his instruments.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}小説[しょうせつ]{や|ya-list}雑誌[ざっし]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed novels, magazines and so on at the library.
why: など follows the last example in an open list of borrowed items.

jp: かぜ{の|no-possessive}とき、熱[ねつ]{や|ya-list}せき{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-subject}出[で]ます。
en: When you have a cold, you get a fever, a cough and so on.
why: など presents fever and cough as examples of the symptoms.

jp: この店[みせ]{で|de-place}ケーキ{や|ya-list}パン{など|nado-etc}{も|mo-also}売[う]っています。
en: This shop also sells cakes, bread and so on.
why: など after the last example, with も adding to the main goods.

jp: 山[やま]{で|de-place}鳥[とり]{や|ya-list}虫[むし]{など|nado-etc}{の|no-possessive}声[こえ]{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: In the mountains I heard the sounds of birds, insects and so on.
why: など ends the list of examples, and の links it to 声.

jp: 姉[あね]{は|wa-topic}ケーキ{や|ya-list}クッキー{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}よく焼[や]きます。
en: My older sister often bakes cakes, cookies and so on.
why: など ends the list of sweets as examples before the object marker.
